title: JavaScript Basics
subtitle: Build Interactive Web Pages
description: Learn the language of the web from the ground up. This course takes you through JavaScript fundamentals — from variables and types to DOM manipulation and API calls.

modules.title: What is JavaScript & How to Set It Up
modules.content:
What is JavaScript?

JavaScript is the programming language that makes websites interactive. Every time you click a button, see a popup, or watch an animation on a website — that's JavaScript at work.

While HTML structures a page and CSS styles it, JavaScript brings it to life. It runs directly in your browser, so there's nothing extra to install for basic use!

Running JavaScript

The easiest way to start is right in your browser:

  1. Open Chrome or any browser
  2. Press F12 (or right-click → Inspect)
  3. Click the Console tab
  4. Type JavaScript code and press Enter!
console.log("Hello, Kumusta!");

For bigger projects, use VS Code (free code editor) and create an HTML file with a script tag:

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
  <h1 id="greeting">Kumusta!</h1>
  <script>
    document.getElementById("greeting").textContent = "Hello, World!";
  </script>
</body>
</html>

You can also use Node.js to run JavaScript outside the browser — great for servers and command-line tools.

Why Learn JavaScript?

  • Web Development — it's essential for any website
  • Mobile Apps — React Native lets you build apps with JS
  • High Demand — Filipino JS developers are in demand locally and abroad
  • Huge Community — tons of free resources and libraries
JavaScript is one of the most versatile languages you can learn. Master it, and you can build websites, apps, servers, and more!
objectives: Understand what JavaScript is and where it's used
Run JavaScript in the browser console
Set up a basic HTML file with JavaScript
Understand why JavaScript is valuable to learn

modules.title: Variables, Types & Operators
modules.content:
Declaring Variables

JavaScript has three ways to declare variables:

let age = 25;        // can be changed
const name = "Ana";  // cannot be reassigned
var old = 10;        // old way — avoid using this

Always prefer const by default. Use let only when you need to change the value later. Avoid var — it has confusing scoping behavior.

Data Types

  • String — text: "Mabuhay" or 'Hello' or `Template`
  • Number — integers and decimals: 42, 3.14
  • Boolean — true or false
  • Null — intentional empty value: null
  • Undefined — not yet assigned: undefined
  • Array — ordered list: [1, 2, 3]
  • Object — key-value pairs: { name: "Ana", age: 25 }

Template Literals

Use backticks for easy string interpolation:

const price = 50;
const qty = 3;
console.log(`Total: ₱${price * qty}`);  // Total: ₱150

Operators

// Arithmetic: +, -, *, /, % (modulo)
console.log(10 % 3);  // 1 (remainder)

// Comparison:
5 == "5"   // true  (loose equality — avoids this)
5 === "5"  // false (strict equality — USE THIS)

// Logical: && (AND), || (OR), ! (NOT)
const age = 20;
const hasID = true;
console.log(age >= 18 && hasID);  // true
Always use === instead of ==. Strict equality avoids surprising type coercion bugs.
objectives: Declare variables using let, const, and understand var
Work with strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, and objects
Use template literals for string interpolation

modules.title: DOM Manipulation
modules.content:
What is the DOM?

The DOM (Document Object Model) is how JavaScript interacts with your HTML page. The browser turns your HTML into a tree of objects, and JavaScript can read and modify this tree.

Selecting Elements

// Get a single element by ID
const header = document.getElementById("main-header");

// Get elements by class name
const cards = document.querySelectorAll(".card");

// Modern way — CSS selector style
const btn = document.querySelector(".submit-btn");

Changing Content

// Change text
header.textContent = "New Title";

// Change HTML (be careful with user input!)
header.innerHTML = "<em>New</em> Title";

// Change styles
header.style.color = "blue";
header.style.fontSize = "24px";

Event Listeners

Events let your code respond to user actions:

const button = document.querySelector("#myBtn");

button.addEventListener("click", function() {
    alert("Button was clicked!");
});

Common events: click, submit, keydown, mouseover, scroll

Practical Example: A Simple Counter

<button id="countBtn">Click me! (0)</button>

<script>
let count = 0;
const btn = document.getElementById("countBtn");

btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    count++;
    btn.textContent = `Click me! (${count})`;
});
</script>

Creating Elements

const newCard = document.createElement("div");
newCard.textContent = "New card content";
newCard.classList.add("card");
document.body.appendChild(newCard);
The DOM is where JavaScript becomes visual. Master DOM manipulation and you can build entire interactive websites!
objectives: Add event listeners for user interactions

modules.title: Async JavaScript & APIs
modules.content:
Why Asynchronous?

JavaScript is single-threaded — it does one thing at a time. But what if you need to fetch data from a server? You don't want your whole page to freeze while waiting.

Asynchronous JavaScript lets you start a task, move on, and handle the result when it's ready.

Callbacks → Promises → Async/Await

Promises represent a future value:

fetch("https://api.example.com/data")
  .then(response => response.json())
  .then(data => console.log(data))
  .catch(error => console.error("Error:", error));

Async/Await is the modern, cleaner way:

async function getData() {
  try {
    const response = await fetch("https://api.example.com/data");
    const data = await response.json();
    console.log(data);
  } catch (error) {
    console.error("Error:", error);
  }
}

getData();

Real Example: Philippine Weather Data

Let's fetch weather info from PAGASA's API:

async function getWeather() {
  const response = await fetch("https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=14.5995&longitude=120.9842¤t_weather=true");
  const data = await response.json();
  const temp = data.current_weather.temperature;
  document.getElementById("temp").textContent = `Temperature in Manila: ${temp}°C`;
}

getWeather();

What is an API?

An API (Application Programming Interface) is a way for programs to talk to each other. Most APIs use JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) — which is just a text format JavaScript can easily parse.

// JSON looks like a JavaScript object
{
  "name": "Juan",
  "city": "Cebu",
  "balance": 15000
}
Async/await makes working with APIs feel like writing normal synchronous code. It's one of the most important patterns in modern JavaScript.
objectives: Understand what APIs and JSON are

questions.question: Which keyword should you use to declare a constant variable in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Use 'const' for values that won't be reassigned. 'let' is for values that change, 'var' is outdated, and 'constant' is not a JavaScript keyword.

questions.question: What is the output of: console.log(5 === "5")?
questions.explanation: The === (strict equality) operator checks both value AND type. 5 is a number, "5" is a string — different types, so it returns false.

questions.question: Which method selects an element by its CSS class name and returns the first match?
questions.explanation: document.querySelector() takes a CSS selector and returns the first matching element. getElementById selects by ID (not class), and querySelectorAll returns all matches.

questions.question: How do you add a click event listener to a button?
questions.explanation: addEventListener is the standard way to attach event handlers in JavaScript. It takes the event type ('click') and a callback function.

questions.question: What does document.querySelector(".card") select?
questions.explanation: querySelector with a CSS selector returns only the first matching element. Use querySelectorAll if you want all matching elements.

questions.question:
What does the following print?

const x = `Hello ${"World"}`;
questions.explanation: Template literals (using backticks) evaluate expressions inside ${}. The string "World" is just the text World.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to define an async function?
questions.explanation: The 'async' keyword is placed before 'function' to create an async function. 'await' is used inside async functions to wait for Promises.

questions.question: What does the fetch() function return?
options: A Promise that resolves to a Response object
The actual data from the API
questions.explanation: fetch() returns a Promise that resolves to a Response object. You need to call .json() on it to get the actual data.
